summary:
This document is a joint resolution. That is a plan that both parts of Congress vote on. In this case, it deals with fighting between the United States and a country called Iran.

The main idea is simple. The people who wrote this bill want the President to pull U.S. troops out of fighting with Iran. They say this fighting was never approved by Congress.

Here is why that matters. The Constitution is the top set of rules for the country. It says only Congress can officially declare war. The bill says Congress never declared war on Iran and never gave special permission to fight there.

The bill lists facts. It says leaders in the government, including the President, have called this fighting a "war." It also says that by April 10, 2026, 13 U.S. troops had died and at least 350 were hurt.

If this becomes law, the President would have to remove U.S. troops from fighting with Iran. The only way troops could stay would be if Congress officially declares war or gives special permission.

But the bill does allow some things. The U.S. could still:
- Defend itself if attacked.
- Gather and share information about threats.
- Help Israel and other countries protect themselves.
- Help U.S. citizens leave the area safely.

Right now this is only an idea. It has been sent to a group of senators to study before any vote.
